long_biography.plain_text:
The Second World War forced Pearl Assurance chairman Sir George Tilley to reconsider how life policies treated death on active service. Pearl kept pre-war ordinary policies free of new restrictions, improved benefits on newer contracts and waived an industrial-policy exclusion so claims from armed-forces service could be paid in full.

Tilley had already made low operating costs and policyholder bonuses recurring themes of Pearl's annual meetings. In 1937 he reported record-low expenses in the industrial branch while maintaining bonuses and investment returns. The Cheltenham native also returned to his home town for company gatherings and civic fundraising, including opening a technical-college fair.
